title: 台湾、「シリコンの盾」に資金流入しやすく　TSMCへの投資上限上げ
extracted_text:
台湾の金融当局は域内の投資信託などに対する単一銘柄への投資上限を引き上げた。対象は半導体大手の 台湾積体電路製造 （TSMC）だ。運用会社の競争力を高める規制緩和策で域内の長期資金が「シリコンの盾」と呼ばれる半導体産業に流入しやすくなる。

金融監督管理委員会（FSC）は4月24日から、域内の株式投資信託やアクティブ型の上場投資信託（ETF）に対する個別株への投資上限を緩和した。従来は個別株投資の上限比率を純資産の10%としていたが、最大25%に引き上げた。

対象は台湾の加権指数構成銘柄の時価総額に占める比率が10%を超える銘柄だ。条件を満たすのはTSMCのみだ。事実上、同社への投資比率の引き上げを念頭に置いた制度改正だ。

FSCは「台湾のテクノロジー産業の急速な発展と、一部の上場企業の時価総額の継続的な増加を考慮した」と説明する。

対象となる投資信託は138本で運用額は約1兆481億台湾ドル（約5兆2000億円）、ETFは14本で運用額は約2310億台湾ドルだ。市場関係者の試算によると、新ルール適用で最大2000億台湾ドル規模の資金がTSMC株に流入する可能性がある。

人工知能（AI）に向けた成長期待に加え、新ルールが追い風となり、TSMC株は27日、最高値を更新した。台湾株に占める時価総額比率は約45%に達する。運用会社は投資上限を上回るTSMC株を売却せざるを得なくなっていた。新ルールは「ファンドの運用の柔軟性を高める」（FSC）狙いがある。

TSMCへの投資配分引き上げは、関連銘柄へのマネー流入も促している。半導体関連の聯華電子（UMC）や日月光投資控股（ASE）は30日終値で23日比それぞれ5%高、3%高だった。

TSMCは米 エヌビディア や米 アップル などが使う最先端の半導体製造を受託している。半導体製造受託における市場シェアは25年に約7割に達した。AIを筆頭に世界のハイテク産業にとって代わりの利かない基盤となっている。

サプライチェーン（供給網）の要となる台湾の半導体産業はシリコンシールド（シリコンの盾）とも呼ばれ、有事への抑止力も期待される。

各国・地域で半導体製造の自国回帰の機運もあり、TSMCは先端工場の海外展開を進めている。米国では第2工場が完成し、第3工場の建設も始まった。生産能力が台湾外に分散すれば、台湾の「盾」を弱めるとの懸念もあった。

米スティムソン・センターのパメラ・ケネディ氏は「TSMCが米国への巨額投資をしても台湾のシリコンシールドを覆さない」と指摘する。台湾内に築いた300社超からなる供給網がTSMCを支えており、米国ですべてを再現することは難しいとみるためだ。

今回の台湾による投資上限引き上げにより、半導体関連銘柄への域内の資金流入は一段と加速している。時価総額の増加は企業の資金調達力を高め、海外投資家からの関心も集めやすくなる。

運用会社にとって投資配分の偏りといったリスクはあるが、株式市場での評価の高まりが「シリコンの盾」を厚くする側面もある点は見逃せない。

translated_text:
Taiwan's financial regulator has raised the investment cap for single stocks for domestic investment trusts and other funds. The target is semiconductor giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). This regulatory easing measure is designed to enhance the competitiveness of asset management firms and will make it easier for long-term domestic capital to flow into the semiconductor industry, often referred to as the "silicon shield."

On April 24, the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) eased the individual stock investment limit for domestic equity investment trusts and active exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Previously, the individual stock investment limit was set at 10% of net assets, but this has been raised to a maximum of 25%.

The targets are stocks that account for more than 10% of the market capitalization of Taiwan's weighted index constituents. TSMC is the only company that meets this condition. This is effectively an institutional reform designed with raising the investment ratio for the company in mind.

The FSC explained that it "took into account the rapid development of Taiwan's technology industry and the continued growth in market capitalization of some listed companies."

The investment trusts subject to this measure number 138 funds with assets under management of approximately NT$1.0481 trillion (about ¥5.02 trillion), and there are 14 ETFs with assets under management of approximately NT$231 billion. According to estimates by market participants, under the new rules, up to NT$200 billion in capital could flow into TSMC shares.

Bolstered by growth expectations centered on artificial intelligence (AI) and aided by the new rules, TSMC shares hit a record high on the 27th. The company's share of Taiwan's total market capitalization has reached approximately 45%. Asset management firms had been forced to sell TSMC shares that exceeded the investment cap. The new rules aim to "enhance flexibility in fund management" (FSC).

The increased TSMC investment allocation is also driving capital flows into related stocks. Semiconductor makers United Microelectronics (UMC) and ASE Technology Holding (ASE) ended the 30th up 5% and 3% respectively from 23 days prior.

TSMC handles cutting-edge semiconductor manufacturing for U.S. companies including NVIDIA and Apple. Its market share in semiconductor contract manufacturing is expected to reach approximately 70% in 2025. It has become an irreplaceable foundation for the global high-tech industry, particularly in AI.

Taiwan's semiconductor industry, which forms the backbone of the supply chain, is also called the silicon shield and is expected to serve as a deterrent in times of crisis.

With countries and regions promoting the reshoring of semiconductor manufacturing, TSMC is expanding its advanced factories overseas. In the United States, a second plant has been completed and construction of a third plant has begun. There were concerns that dispersing production capacity outside Taiwan would weaken Taiwan's "shield."

Pamela Kennedy of the Stimson Center noted that "even if TSMC makes massive investments in the United States, it will not overturn Taiwan's silicon shield." This is because the company's supply network built in Taiwan with more than 300 suppliers supports TSMC, making it difficult to replicate everything in the U.S.

With Taiwan raising the investment cap, domestic capital flows into semiconductor stocks are accelerating further. The increase in market capitalization enhances companies' fundraising capabilities and makes them more attractive to foreign investors.

While there are risks for asset management firms, such as investment concentration, it is also important not to overlook that higher valuations in the stock market can thicken the "silicon shield."
title_en: Taiwan Eases Capital Flow to "Silicon Shield" - Raises Investment Cap for TSMC
